_doc: Registro de paridade. Cada recurso visível ao usuário tem um id; para cada plataforma marcada "yes" o código precisa de um comentário `// parity: <id>` no arquivo que implementa. "no" = falta (precisa de note). "n/a" = não se aplica à plataforma. Rode scripts/parity.py (o CI roda).

platform_strings.why: Nome do sistema / da máquina e atalhos (⌘S × Ctrl+S, barra de menus × bandeja, Finder × .exe)
mac: Changes wait for Save (⌘S). You'll be asked before leaving a profile with unsaved changes.
Favorites (shown in the menu bar while this device is connected)
Changes the menu bar icon and the logo inside the app. The Finder/Dock icon is the wave.
Reduce Motion is on in System Settings, so animations stay off.
On the other machine choose "Connect to a server", click Find on my network (or type the address) and enter the code. Syncs only while this Mac is on.
When the app runs (or is focused) and this device is the output, its profile takes over. When it quits, the device goes back to its selected/default profile.
windows: Changes wait for Save (Ctrl+S). You'll be asked before leaving a profile with unsaved changes.
Favorites (shown in the tray panel while this device is connected)
Changes the tray icon and the logo inside the app. The .exe icon is the wave.
Animation effects are off in Windows settings, so animations stay off.
On the other machine choose "Connect to a server", find this PC (or type the address) and enter the code. Windows Firewall will ask to allow MyOwnEQ on private networks.
When the app runs (or is focused) and this device is the output, its profile takes over. Rules made on the Mac need the Windows .exe filled in.

platform_strings.why: Motor de áudio: Core Audio (limitador próprio, permissão) × Equalizer APO (sem limitador)
mac: Boost on: the limiter is forced on, so it gets louder without ever clipping. Very high boost squashes loud parts.
Could not create the system audio tap. Allow MyOwnEQ under System Settings › Privacy & Security › Screen & System Audio Recording.
windows: Windows engine (Equalizer APO) has no limiter: auto preamp keeps it from clipping.
Equalizer APO is not installed. MyOwnEQ uses it as the Windows audio engine (free, open source).
1. Install it  2. In its Configurator, tick the outputs you use  3. Reboot if it asks  4. Click Check again.
Can't write to %@. Allow it once (Windows will ask for admin).
Equalizer APO found. Let MyOwnEQ manage it?
Your current config.txt is backed up as %@. “Take over” turns off other EQ (e.g. Peace) so you don't get double EQ; “Keep mine” adds MyOwnEQ on top.
Restored your previous Equalizer APO config
Equalizer APO isn't enabled on “%@”, so the EQ does nothing there.
Open Device selector, tick “%@” and restart Windows. Bluetooth headphones: also open “Troubleshooting options” and try “Install APO as SFX/EFX (experimental)”.
The MyOwnEQ engine couldn't start (%@). Using Equalizer APO's filters.
The MyOwnEQ engine isn't processing audio on this output. Switched back to Equalizer APO's filters.
Boost uses the MyOwnEQ engine's limiter, so it never clips.
Boost needs the MyOwnEQ engine (Preferences › Windows audio engine): Equalizer APO alone has no limiter.
Runs MyOwnEQ's own DSP inside Equalizer APO: same sound as the Mac, a real limiter (so boost works) and instant previews. If it doesn't process audio, the app switches back by itself.
MyOwnEQ engine loaded, waiting for audio
MyOwnEQ engine not loaded yet (play something; Equalizer APO loads it with the audio)

windows: Find it in the taskbar corner (click ^ if hidden). Tip: drag the icon next to the clock to keep it visible.
